design_rationale: The study is a prospective randomized trial where eligible patients were randomly assigned to treatment groups using a central registration office and a computer-generated list.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated sequence was used and allocation was centrally concealed until after registration via facsimile, resulting in well-balanced baseline characteristics between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The investigators sent a registration form describing the clinical characteristics of eligible patients to the registration office by facsimile. Immediately after registration, the registration office randomly assigned the subject to either treatment group using a computer-generated list and informed the investigators of the treatment assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although open-label, the intervention evaluated treatment strategies/goals, deviations reflected standard clinical management per protocol, and analysis was conducted on an intention-to-treat basis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The effects of the two treatments were compared according to the intention to treat.

domain_judgments.rationale: Loss to follow-up was very low (less than 2% in each group) and balanced between groups, making it unlikely to introduce bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Follow-up inquiries were sent to the subjects who had discontinued treatment; responses were not obtained from 35 subjects (1.6%) in the strict-treatment group and 38 (1.7%) in the mild-treatment group (p = 0.71; Fig. 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were well-defined clinical events adjudicated by an independent endpoint committee that was blinded to group assignment and blood pressure trends.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Endpoints were evaluated by the members of the Endpoint Evaluation Committee, who were blinded to the treatment assignments and the time course of BP.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered prospectively, followed an earlier published protocol, and reported all prespecified primary and secondary outcomes without evidence of selective outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This study was registered at the UMIN Clinical Trial Registry with the trial number UMIN000001021. The methods, protocol, and interim data monitoring of this trial have been reported elsewhere (15).

overall_summary: The trial was judged to have a low risk of bias across all domains. Central randomization with allocation concealment was used, endpoint adjudication was blinded (PROBE design), missing outcome data were minimal, and results were analyzed and reported per a prespecified protocol.

paper_title: 5cc35d56_J of Clinical Hypertension - 2013 - Wei - Effects of Intensive Antihypertensive Treatment on Chinese Hypertensive Patients
design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to intensive or standard antihypertensive treatment using a computer-generated table of random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: While a computer-generated random number table was used for sequence generation, the method of allocation concealment is not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 724 hypertensive patients older than 70 years were randomly assigned to either intensive antihypertensive treatment or standard treatment by using a computer-generated table of random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was open-label by design (PROBE) to titration targets, but intervention protocols were standardized and an intention-to-treat analysis was performed without evidence of substantial unbalanced deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This was a prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded-endpoint assessment (PROBE) study... An intent-to-treat analysis was performed to ensure that all study participants were followed until the conclusion of the study, irrespective of whether the participant was still receiving or complying with the treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: All randomized patients were accounted for across the trial profile (Figure 2 shows 363 randomized in the intensive group and 361 in the standard group, all followed and analyzed with censoring for the few lost/died).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants who were lost to follow-up or died of other causes were censored and were also included in the final analyses for the actual follow-up period.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary and secondary outcomes were evaluated by a blinded Endpoint Evaluation Committee using objective criteria.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In order to reduce investigation bias, endpoints were evaluated by the members of the Endpoint Evaluation Committee, who were blinded to the treatment assignments and the time course of BP.

domain_judgments.rationale: No mention of a prospective trial registration number or pre-specified statistical analysis protocol is provided to rule out selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint was the combined incidence of fatal/nonfatal stroke, acute myocardial infarction, and other cardiovascular deaths (sudden death and heart failure death)... Secondary endpoints were deaths from any causes.

overall_summary: The study is judged to have some concerns overall due to lack of details regarding allocation concealment in the randomization process and absence of a trial registration or pre-published analysis protocol.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to treatment groups using a central computerized Web-based randomization program stratified by clinical center.

domain_judgments.rationale: Central web-based computerized randomization was used to conceal allocation, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was performed with the use of a central computerized randomization program on a Web-based interface, with stratification according to clinical center.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the trial was open-label (which is typical and necessary for treat-to-target blood pressure trials), treatment algorithms were prespecified, adherence was monitored, and analyses followed an intention-to-treat principle.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Investigators and patients were aware of the trial-group assignments... All analyses were based on the intention-to-treat approach, and all models were adjusted for clinical center.

domain_judgments.rationale: Loss to follow-up was very low (2.7% overall) and balanced across groups, with survival/time-to-event analyses properly censoring lost participants.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 234 patients (2.7%) were lost to follow-up before the end of the trial... Patients who were lost to follow-up were included in the final analysis, with data censored at the time of the last follow-up visit.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary and secondary clinical outcomes were assessed using standardized definitions and adjudicated by an outcome committee blinded to trial-group assignments.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Definitions and ascertainment criteria for the trial outcomes are provided in Table S1. Members of the adjudication committee were unaware of the trial-group assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT03015311) with a prespecified statistical analysis plan and stopping boundaries that guided the early termination.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The complete statistical analysis plan is included in the Supplementary Appendix... Prespecified interim analyses were performed by the data and safety monitoring committee at the end of each year. The O’Brien–Fleming alpha-spending function was used to maintain the overall type I error rate of 0.05 across these repeated analyses.

overall_summary: The study is a well-conducted, large multicenter randomized controlled trial with robust central allocation concealment, low missing data, blinded adjudication of cardiovascular outcomes, and adherence to a prespecified analysis plan with formal stopping boundaries.

design_rationale: The study is described as a multicenter, parallel-group, prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded end point trial where patients were randomly assigned by the VALISH Data Center.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization was centrally managed by the VALISH Data Center with stratification/minimization, concealment of allocation is ensured by central assignment, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: the patients were randomly assigned by the VALISH Data Center according to the following factors; sex, age (<75 or >=75 years), systolic BP (<175 or >=175 mm Hg), antihypertensive therapy, and institution (weighting coefficient: 2).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although this was an open-label trial comparing blood pressure targets, the treatment protocol allowed titration and add-on medications according to assignment, deviations reflected target-driven clinical care, and the primary analysis was based on intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All of the registered study patients assigned to treatment were analyzed on an intentionto-treat basis. In addition, a per-protocol analysis was performed.

domain_judgments.rationale: Loss to follow-up was low (181/3260, ~5.5%), balanced between groups, and survival time was censored appropriately in the time-to-event analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In total, 3260 patients from 461 centers in Japan were registered from February 2004 to August 2005 and then randomly assigned to either the strict control group or the moderate control group. Because 181 patients were lost to follow-up, 3079 were followed up until March 2008 or for >=2.5 years (Figure 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial utilized a prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded end point (PROBE) design where an independent endpoint committee blinded to treatment assignment adjudicated clinical outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: End points and adverse events were blindly evaluated according to the prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded end point design by the endpoint committee and the safety committee, respectively.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study design, primary composite endpoint, and secondary endpoints were prespecified in a published design paper and analyzed according to an approved statistical analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Statistical analysis was performed by Shin Nippon Biomedical Laboratories, Ltd according to the statistical analysis plan approved by the statistics committee (see Appendix).

overall_summary: All five domains were assessed as low risk of bias due to sound central randomization, adherence to an intention-to-treat approach, minimal missing outcome data, blinded adjudication of endpoints (PROBE design), and prespecified reporting according to an approved statistical analysis plan.
